source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 11: Verify (AB)^t = B^tA^t, parts (i)-(ii) (book page 61).

blocks.explanation:
We must check the reversal law for transposes on given matrices.
Plan: compute \(AB\) and transpose it; compute \(B^{t}\), \(A^{t}\) and their product; compare.
steps:
Given: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
To verify: \((AB)^{t} = B^{t}A^{t}\)
Method: Work out the left side and the right side separately and compare entry by entry. Note the order reverses: \(B^{t}\) comes first.

Left side: transpose of \(AB\)
\[(AB)^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 9 \\ 5 & 7 \end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Rows of \(AB\) become columns.

Write \(B^{t}\) and \(A^{t}\)
\[B^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[A^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ -1 & -3 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Rows become columns in each matrix.

Compare
\[(AB)^{t} = B^{t}A^{t} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides have the same order and the same entries in every position.

blocks.explanation:
The same reversal law with a \(3 \times 2\) matrix \(A\) and a \(2 \times 2\) matrix \(B\).
Plan: left side \((AB)^{t}\), right side \(B^{t}A^{t}\), compare.
steps:
Given: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\), \(B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\)
To verify: \((AB)^{t} = B^{t}A^{t}\)
Method: Work out the left side and the right side separately and compare entry by entry. Note the order reverses: \(B^{t}\) comes first.

Left side: transpose of \(AB\)
\[(AB)^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & -7 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & -5 \end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Rows of \(AB\) become columns.

Write \(B^{t}\) and \(A^{t}\)
\[B^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -2 \\ -3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[A^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\]
Why: Rows become columns in each matrix.

Compare
\[(AB)^{t} = B^{t}A^{t} \;\checkmark\]
Why: Both sides have the same order and the same entries in every position.
